{{Short description|Canadian mathematician (born 1942)}}
'''John Stephen Halperin''' (born 1 February 1942 in [[Kingston, Ontario]])<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004 </ref> is a Canadian mathematician who deals with differential geometry and algebraic topology.

A son of the mathematician [[Israel Halperin]], Stephen Halperin studied at the [[University of Toronto]] with a bachelor's degree in 1966 and a master's degree in 1967. He received in 1970 his PhD from [[Cornell University]] under the supervision of [[Hsien Chung Wang]] with thesis ''Real Cohomology and Smooth Transformation Groups''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id = 16281|name=J. Stephen (John) Halperin}}</ref> He then became an assistant professor and in 1979 a full professor at the University of Toronto.

Halperin was a visiting scholar in 1981 at the [[University of Bonn]], in 1986 at the [[Université Nice-Sophia-Antipolis|University of Nice]], and in 1995 at the [[University of Lille]].

His research deals with homotopy theory and homology of [[loop space]]s with applications in geometry. He wrote a three-volume textbook on differential geometry with Werner H. Greub and Ray Vanstone.

In 1984 Halperin was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]]. In 1997 he received the [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]]. 

In 1999 he became a full professor at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], where he served as the dean of the College of Computer, Mathematical and Physical Sciences.

==Selected publications==
* with Ray Vanstone and Werner H. Greub: '' Connections, Curvature and Cohomology '', 3 volumes (Volume 1: De Rham Cohomology of Manifolds and Vector Bundles, Volume 2 Lie Groups, Principal Bundles and Characteristic Classes, Volume 3 Cohomology of principal bundles and homogeneous spaces), Academic Press 1972, 1973, 1976<ref>{{cite journal|author=Samelson, H.|authorlink=Hans Samelson|title=Review of ''Connection, curvature, and cohomology'' by Werner Greub, Stephen Halperin and Ray Vanstone|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]|year=1977|volume=83|issue=5|pages=1011–1015|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1977-83-05/S0002-9904-1977-14358-9/S0002-9904-1977-14358-9.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1977-14358-9|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* with Yves Félix: [https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1982-273-01/S0002-9947-1982-0664027-0/S0002-9947-1982-0664027-0.pdf '' Rational L.-S. category and its applications ''], [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 273, 1982, 1–38
* with [[Karsten Grove]]: '' Contributions of rational homotopy theory to global problems in geometry '', [[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]], vol. 56, 1982, 171–177 {{doi|10.1007/BF02700465}}
* [http://www.numdam.org/item/MSMF_1983_2_9-10__1_0/ ''Lectures on minimal models''], Mémoires de la Société Mathématique de France, 2<sup>e</sup> série, tome 9–10, 1983, 1–261
* with Yves Félix and Jean-Claude Thomas: [https://books.google.com/books?id=xoM5DxQZihQC&pg=PA829 ''Differential graded algebras in topology''], in [[Ioan James|I.M. James]] (editor) '' Handbook in Algebraic Topology '', Elsevier Science 1995, Chapter 16, pp. 829–865.
* with Yves Félix and Jean-Claude Thomas: [https://books.google.com/books?id=HLzICw143J4C ''Rational Homotopy Theory''], [[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]], Springer Verlag 2001
